| [LIT-018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-018.md) v3 | Distinguishability and Accessible Information in Quantum Theory | Fuchs (1995), [arXiv:quant-ph/9601020](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/9601020). Minimizing the Bhattacharyya overlap Σ_b √(tr ρ0E_b)√(tr ρ1E_b) over all POVMs gives exactly F(ρ0,ρ1) = tr√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2}) (Eq. 3.28). The minimum is attained by a projective measurement in the eigenbasis of M = ρ1^{-1/2}√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2})ρ1^{-1/2} (Eq. 3.67). For binary ensembles, the same Schwarz-inequality technique gives three results: a short proof of the Holevo bound I(t) ≤ S(t), with equality iff [ρ0,ρ1] = 0 (Eq. 3.149); a tighter upper bound L(t) (Eq. 3.187, integrated in Eqs. 3.230/3.244; closed form for qubits in Eq. 3.269); and a measurement-attained lower bound M(t) = tr[(1−t)ρ0 ln L_ρ(ρ0) + tρ1 ln L_ρ(ρ1)] (Eq. 3.203). The thesis also proves that two states can be broadcast iff they commute, and cloned iff they are identical or orthogonal (§4.3, proof written for invertible ρ0, ρ1). | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-021); still the most self-contained derivation of mixed-state fidelity as an optimal classical overlap, and of the Holevo bound by the curvature (J'' vs S'') argument. Read §3.3 and §3.5.1–3.5.2 for those, and Ch. 2 as a tutorial on why error probability, the Chernoff bound, KL and mutual information are the operationally grounded classical measures. The quantum-Kullback bounds (§3.6), the inference–disturbance formalism (§4.2) and the no-broadcasting proof (§4.3) are preliminary or appeared in companion papers. Read those papers for their final forms. |
| [LIT-041](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-041.md) | The Work Capacity of Channels with Memory: Maximum Extractable Work in Percept-Action Loops | Fiderer et al. (2025), [ARXIV-2504.06209](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.06209). When an agent's actions change what it later perceives, the maximum rate at which it can extract work from its environment (the environment channel's "work capacity") is in general reached neither by a maximally predictive agent nor by one that randomizes its actions and forgets them. Prediction and forgetting have to be traded off. | Deferred — seeded from the abstract and a skim on 2026-09-25; not read in full |
| [LIT-042](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-042.md) | Shannon invariants: A scalable approach to information decomposition | Gutknecht et al. (2025), [ARXIV-2504.15779](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.15779). Two averages over the partial information decomposition can be computed from Shannon entropies alone, with the number of entropies growing linearly in the number of sources. These are the average degree of redundancy and the average degree of vulnerability. They sidestep PID's ambiguous choice of redundancy measure and its super-exponential cost, explain what the old redundancy–synergy index actually measures, and show redundancy increasing and vulnerability decreasing with depth and training in small quantised networks. | Deferred — seeded from the abstract and a skim on 2026-09-25; not read in full |

| [LIT-053](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-053.md) | The Homological Nature of Entropy | Baudot et al. (2015), DOI-10.3390/e17053253. Shannon entropy is the (first) universal cohomology class of an "information structure" built from a family of observables and a family of probability laws. The same holds for quantum probabilities and for dynamic observation trees, which gives a topology of information that recovers multivariate mutual informations and KL divergence. | Deferred — seeded from the abstract on 2026-09-25; not read in full |
| [LIT-058](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-058.md) | Mutual Information and Minimum Mean-square Error in Gaussian Channels | Guo et al. (2004), [arXiv:cs/0412108](https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/0412108). For any finite-power input observed in additive Gaussian noise, the derivative of the input–output mutual information (in nats) with respect to SNR equals half the MMSE, whatever the input distribution (the I-MMSE identity). A consequence is that the causal filtering MMSE equals the average of the non-causal smoothing MMSE over SNRs uniform on [0, snr]. | Deferred — seeded from the abstract and a skim on 2026-09-25; not read in full |
